verdict.rationale: Solid's documented model splits state into an explicit accessor and setter, and only the code that depends on a piece of state reruns. That gives predictable, traceable updates, and a year-long production user reports state changes are intuitive and easy to debug. However, the evidence never explicitly documents one-way data flow or contrasts it with two-way binding, and one hands-on report calls the dev tools alpha/unusable, which weakens the 'trace state changes' part. missing for 10: first-party documentation of unidirectional data flow / no two-way binding, usable tooling for tracing reactive updates.

support.subject: As a developer, I can trace state changes through explicit, predictable data flow instead of debugging implicit two-way bindings

citations.quote: Create a piece of reactive state, giving us an accessor, count(), and a setter, setCount()
when a piece of state changes, only the code that depends on it will rerun.
They value that everything in the reactive system is immediate, which keeps state changes intuitive and easy to debug.
